recent_posts.title: We're organizing a conference
recent_posts.summary: Convex is announcing Abstract, a conference about principled design scheduled for September 2nd, 2026 at SFJAZZ Center in San Francisco. The event will feature builders and designers from various disciplines — not just SaaS — discussing the principles behind their work. Convex is accepting no paid sponsorships to ensure the most interesting voices are featured. A waiting list is now open at abstract.convex.dev.

recent_posts.title: Convex Open Source Recap 2025
recent_posts.summary: Convex recaps its 2025 open source contributions as part of the Open Source Pledge, reporting $5,454 per developer in sponsorships — well above the $2,000 minimum. Major contributions include $50,000 to TanStack and covering ClawHub's hosting bill in perpetuity. Additional sponsored projects include Tailwind, Biome, Tokio, Vite, Zod, SolidJS, Hono, PyO3, cargo-nextest, and others chosen by the engineering team.

recent_posts.title: Convex for Enterprise (and updates to everything else)
recent_posts.summary: Convex is launching enterprise plans targeting larger teams and companies migrating onto the platform. Two new tiers are introduced: a Business Plan at $2,500/month with no annual commitment, and a custom Enterprise Plan with annual contracts and precommit discounts. Both include dedicated infrastructure, SSO, audit logging, fine-grained access policies, SLAs, and compliance reports. Alongside the enterprise launch, Convex is updating its self-serve Free, Starter, and Pro plans: concurrent deployments increase from 120 to 300, file bandwidth pricing is replaced with a cheaper data egress metric at $0.11/GB (nearly 3x cheaper), and vector bandwidth is replaced with a clearer Search Queries metric. Network ingress becomes free. Most existing customers will see lower bills. Changes roll out in May.

recent_posts.title: Convex launches EU hosting in AWS eu-west-1 region
recent_posts.summary: Convex now offers EU hosting in AWS eu-west-1 region for customers with regulatory and compliance requirements. EU deployments can be created through the Convex Dashboard or Management API, with CLI support coming next week. The service is available on all plans including free tier, though paid plans have 30% higher pricing due to AWS costs. Existing deployments require backup and restore to migrate regions. Canada and Australia regions are planned next.

recent_posts.title: Convex Open Source Update
recent_posts.summary: Convex announces a formal program offering credits to open source projects and launches a landing page showcasing sponsored projects. The company continues its commitment to open source by gradually releasing more platform components for self-hosting, building on previous initiatives like releasing Chef and joining the Open Source Pledge. Open source projects can now apply for Convex credits, with priority given to projects Convex depends on.

recent_posts.title: Convex 1.31.0 changes ctx.db API to require explicit table names
recent_posts.summary: Convex 1.31.0 introduces a breaking API change where db.get, db.patch, db.replace, and db.delete now require the table name as the first argument. This change improves API consistency, enhances security by preventing cross-table ID vulnerabilities, and paves the way for custom document IDs. Existing code remains functional but should be migrated using the provided ESLint plugin or standalone codemod tool, which automatically infer table names from TypeScript types.

recent_posts.title: Product Updates - Volume 25
recent_posts.summary: Convex announces several platform updates including preview deployments now available on free accounts, a new "Copy as Markdown" feature in documentation, enhanced CLI protection for large index deletions, file exclusion options for backups, cryptographic signatures for webhook log streams, column management in the dashboard, ESLint plugin out of beta, improved validator methods in the NPM package, and Zod 4 support in convex-helpers.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Components Authoring
recent_posts.summary: Convex has made its Components Authoring APIs generally available, allowing developers to build and publish reusable backend modules that execute transactionally. The release includes an authoring guide, three new components (WorkOS, NeutralBase, and Stripe), and a Components Directory registry. Convex is also launching an authoring challenge to encourage community contributions and ecosystem growth around modular backend solutions.

recent_posts.title: Convex Vercel Marketplace Integration
recent_posts.summary: Convex is now available on the Vercel Marketplace, enabling one-click installation directly from the Vercel dashboard. The integration provides developers with type-safe APIs, realtime synchronization between frontend and backend, transactional guarantees without SQL, automatic caching with strong consistency, and access to the Convex components ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: Convex raises $24M to reinvent backends
recent_posts.summary: Convex announced a $24M Series A funding round led by a16z and Spark Capital to scale their backend platform. The company has grown 10x in customer base and revenue over nine months, with customers ranging from hackathon teams to enterprises. The funding will support hiring, developing new features like OLAP support and local-first sync, and building a sustainable, profitable business. Convex plans to enhance their component marketplace, improve their open-source self-hosted edition, and optimize infrastructure costs to ensure long-term viability for customers building on their platform.

top_posts.title: Open Kitchen: Chef is now OSS
top_posts.summary: Convex has open-sourced Chef, their LLM-driven code generation tool that has been used by over 250,000 developers to create full-stack projects. Originally developed as a learning tool for Convex, Chef is now available under Apache 2 license for anyone to use, modify, or fork. Additionally, Convex has expanded their open source sponsorship program beyond TanStack Start to support 12 additional projects and maintainers including ArkType, Biome, Hono, SolidJS, Vite, and Zod.
